title: Auto-Generated SDK
description: Streamline frontend development by automatically generating typed SDKs from your bro.js API.

# Auto-Generated SDK

Why write frontend `fetch` wrappers when the backend already knows what your endpoints are? 

## The Magic Command

Run the following command in your terminal:

```bash
bro sdk
```

`bro.js` will instantly parse your `routes/` folder and generate a `bro-sdk.js` file right in your directory.

## Using the Client

The generated client is a pure vanilla JavaScript `fetch` wrapper. It perfectly maps to your API structure.

```javascript
import { api, setBaseURL, setTokenKey, setLocale } from './bro-sdk.js';

// Setup (optional, defaults to localhost:5000 and 'bro_token')
setBaseURL('https://api.myproduction.com');
setTokenKey('my_custom_token_key');
setLocale('fr'); // Sends Accept-Language: fr

// The client automatically checks localStorage for your JWT
// and attaches it as a Bearer token!

async function fetchUsers() {
  // Standard dot-notation calls. Maps to `GET /users?page=1`
  const users = await api.users.get({ page: 1 });
  console.log(users);
}

async function fetchUserPosts() {
  // Parameterized segment invocations. Maps to `GET /users/:userId/posts`
  const posts = await api.users.userId('123').posts.get();
  console.log(posts);
}

async function login(email, password) {
  // Maps to `POST /auth/login`
  // Automatically stringifies the body and sets Content-Type!
  const response = await api.auth.login.post({ email, password });
  
  // Save the token, the client will use it automatically on the next request
  localStorage.setItem('my_custom_token_key', response.token);
}
```
